html:
A great public hall on the north side of the Roman Forum, rebuilt from 55 BCE by Lucius Aemilius Paullus and finished by his son in 34 BCE.

A basilica in Rome was a roofed hall with rows of columns, used for business, banking and law courts. The first hall on this spot went up in 179 BCE, and the Aemilii family kept rebuilding it as their monument. The rebuilding begun in 55 BCE was paid for in part by Julius Caesar, who was busy winning friends and building his own Forum of Caesar next door.

It burned in 14 BCE and was rebuilt with help from Augustus. Pliny the Elder counted it among the most beautiful buildings in the world. It burned again when the Goths took Rome in 410 (see Sack of Rome); coins melted into its floor in that fire can still be seen.

Only foundations, column stumps and pieces of a carved frieze survive. Its long hall with side aisles became the model for early Christian churches.
sum: A great public hall on the north side of the Roman Forum, rebuilt from 55 BCE by Lucius Aemilius Paullus and finished by his son in 34 BCE.
